story.title: Murder Trial for Tupac Shakur Opens 30 Years After His Death
story.summary: The murder trial for Tupac Shakur has commenced nearly 30 years after the rapper was killed in a drive-by shooting in Las Vegas. Prosecutors allege that a former street gang leader, known as 'Keffe D,' orchestrated the attack as an act of revenge for the beating of his nephew. The trial marks a significant development in a case that has long been considered one of the most prominent cold cases in the U.S.

timeline_highlights.summary: Ukraine launched one of its largest drone attacks against Russia, targeting Moscow and nearby areas, which resulted in at least six fatalities. Concurrently, drone and missile strikes across both Russia and Ukraine led to additional civilian casualties, with reports indicating a total of at least 19 deaths from the combined attacks over the weekend.

event_overview.title: About Gaza Peace Deal
event_overview.subject: Gaza Peace Deal
event_overview.summary: The Gaza Peace Deal refers to the U.S.-backed, internationally supported framework to end the Israel-Hamas war in Gaza through a ceasefire, hostage and detainee releases, Hamas’s disarmament and Gaza’s demilitarization, Israeli withdrawals tied to agreed milestones, humanitarian access, and postwar governance and reconstruction. It builds on earlier Egypt-, Qatar-, and U.S.-mediated ceasefire efforts, but its implementation depends on compliance and verification by multiple parties rather than on a single self-executing agreement.

facts.label: Framework and international status
facts.value: President Trump’s Comprehensive Plan is a 20-point roadmap; the United Nations Security Council endorsed the plan in Resolution 2803 (2025) and welcomed a Board of Peace to support its implementation.

facts.label: Core proposed exchange and military step
facts.value: The framework envisages an end to military operations and a staged Israeli withdrawal, alongside the return of hostages and the release of specified Palestinian detainees; further withdrawal is linked to agreed demilitarization standards, milestones, and timeframes.

facts.label: Disarmament and transitional governance
facts.value: A subsequent 15-point implementation roadmap, presented by Egypt, Qatar, Türkiye, the United States, and the High Representative for Gaza, calls for Hamas to end military, policing, and administrative activity and for the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG) to serve as the transitional civilian authority.

facts.label: Institutions and outside roles
facts.value: The plan’s implementation architecture includes the Board of Peace, an Office of the High Representative for Gaza, the NCAG, and an International Stabilization Force intended to support security, demilitarization, aid delivery, and reconstruction. Egypt, Qatar, Türkiye, and the United States are identified as guarantors in the UN implementation report.

facts.label: Legal and humanitarian context
facts.value: The International Committee of the Red Cross considers Gaza occupied territory under its effective-control assessment and states that international humanitarian law continues to govern protections for civilians and duties relevant to the territory’s administration and supply.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows reported late-July to mid-August 2026 developments concerning the deal’s implementation, Israeli-Hamas military and political responses, and one related Lebanon escalation; it is not a complete chronology of the Gaza war, all negotiations, humanitarian conditions, or the wider regional conflict.

explore_lenses.label: What evidence will the jury weigh?
explore_lenses.title: A case centered on Davis’s own accounts
explore_lenses.summary: Prosecutors are building the case around Duane “Keffe D” Davis’s recorded statements and co-authored memoir; the defense says those accounts are unreliable and unsupported by hard evidence.

claims.text: Prosecutors told jurors that Davis planned a retaliatory shooting after his nephew, Orlando Anderson, was beaten at the MGM Grand, although they do not allege Davis fired the shots.
The prosecution played material from Davis’s 2008 interview and plans to use his 2019 co-authored memoir, which it says describes him handing a gun to men in the back seat of the Cadillac.
Defense lawyer Michael Sanft called the prosecution’s account “fiction,” arguing that investigators’ work was biased, sloppy, and incomplete and that the passage of time impairs recollection.
Authorities have said neither the white Cadillac nor the gun used in the shooting was recovered, and the three other men allegedly in the Cadillac have died.

explore_lenses.label: Why did charges come nearly 30 years later?
explore_lenses.title: Public statements revived a cold case
explore_lenses.summary: The case remained uncharged for decades, then investigators and prosecutors focused on Davis’s repeated public descriptions of the shooting and his alleged role in it.

claims.text: Davis was indicted in 2023, making him the first person charged in Shakur’s killing; the case had previously been a long-running cold case.

A Clark County grand-jury transcript records testimony that Las Vegas police had not given Davis immunity from prosecution, despite his earlier discussions with California-linked law-enforcement personnel.
Judge Carli Kierny ruled that Davis’s 2008 police interview could be used at trial; Sanft had argued detectives promised it would not be used against him.

Prosecutors argue that Davis’s later decision to publish a memoir and discuss the case publicly undercuts his claim that the earlier interview should be excluded; the defense says the memoir was fictionalized for profit.

explore_lenses.summary: The trial is expected to turn on testimony, recordings, and documentary evidence before jurors determine whether Davis was criminally responsible for planning the killing.

story_report.summary: A murder trial has opened in the 1996 drive-by killing of Tupac Shakur, nearly 30 years after the rapper was shot. Prosecutors allege Duane “Keffe D” Davis ordered a retaliatory attack after his nephew, Orlando Anderson, was beaten at the MGM Grand; they do not contend Davis fired the shots. Davis, the first person charged in the long-running cold case, has pleaded not guilty and could face life in prison without parole if convicted.

sections.heading: Prosecutors Detail Davis’s Alleged Role
sections.body: Prosecutors played material from Davis’s 2008 interview and plan to rely on his 2019 co-authored memoir. They say those accounts describe Davis handing a gun to men seated in the back of a Cadillac before the shooting. Authorities have said neither the white Cadillac nor the weapon was recovered, while the three other men allegedly in the vehicle have died.

sections.heading: Defense Challenges Evidence Against Davis
sections.body: Defense lawyer Michael Sanft called the prosecution’s account “fiction,” arguing that the investigation was biased, sloppy and incomplete and that the passage of time has weakened recollections. Sanft had also argued that detectives promised Davis his 2008 interview would not be used against him, but Judge Carli Kierny ruled it admissible. Prosecutors say Davis’s later memoir and public comments weaken that argument; the defense says the memoir was fictionalized for profit.

sections.heading: Jury Faces Month-Long Davis Trial
sections.body: The Associated Press reported that prosecutors planned to call about 35 to 45 witnesses and expected the trial to last roughly a month. The prosecution’s theory does not require it to establish that Davis fired the fatal shots, and the shooter’s identity could remain unresolved even if jurors conclude Davis organized or assisted the attack.

unresolved.text: Jurors must determine what weight to give Davis’s interview statements and memoir, including whether they are accurate admissions, embellishment or both, and whether the remaining evidence proves his alleged role beyond a reasonable doubt.
No verdict date is fixed; the outcome depends on jurors’ assessment of admissible evidence and witness credibility.
